faceless_rules: Muted-readable in the first two seconds.
Typography, handwritten marks, owned book objects, or already-cleared Remotion compositions only.
Do not download retailer covers. Do not use adaptation stills.
Stance is Researched unless a later Read record exists. Never imply personal reading.
One honest reservation in every recommendation.

briefs.title: The Player of Games
briefs.author: Iain M. Banks
briefs.hook: Want the Culture without a giant primer?
briefs.choice: The game, or the whole map?
briefs.who_for: Readers who like politics and games more than a 100-page tour of the setting.
briefs.distinctive: One player, one hostile society, one game that decides the rule.
briefs.reservation: If you want intimate character psychology first, start elsewhere.
beats: Start here, not with the whole series map.
Then decide if you want more Culture.
briefs.rights: Illustrated stills plus already-cleared Orbit jacket overlay. No retailer download.
briefs.schedule_note: Posted early on 18 August as an extra. Keep the 19-25 August 19:30 week and the 13:00 bank on their dated rows. Do not upload this MP4 again.
briefs.do_not: Do not say favourite or I loved. Do not rank the Culture. Do not upload this MP4 a second time.

briefs.title: Team of Rivals
briefs.author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
briefs.hook: A cabinet of opponents, not a greatest-hits Lincoln.
briefs.who_for: Readers who want political biography with a usable structure.
briefs.distinctive: The book is about how Lincoln used rivals, not a shrine.
briefs.reservation: It is long. Treat it as a study of a working method, not a weekend read.
briefs.rights: Illustrated stills plus already-cleared Team of Rivals jacket overlay. No retailer download.
briefs.schedule_note: Posted early on 18 August as a format-test extra. Keep the 20 August dated row. Do not upload this MP4 again.
briefs.do_not: Do not imply every presidential title was personally read. Do not upload this MP4 a second time.

briefs.title: Foster
briefs.author: Claire Keegan
briefs.hook: A short book you can finish tonight and still think about next week.
briefs.who_for: Readers who want literary fiction without a 400-page commitment.
briefs.distinctive: A girl sent to a farm for a summer; warmth, then the secret the house was not supposed to have.
briefs.reservation: It is slight on plot. If you need incident every chapter, this will feel too quiet.
briefs.rights: Typography or handwritten Remotion only until an owned physical copy is photographed. No retailer cover. No Quiet Girl stills.
briefs.do_not: Do not sell the film. Do not quote the novella.

briefs.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
briefs.author: John le Carré
briefs.hook: A spy novel where the violence is in the office, not the chase.
briefs.who_for: Readers who want a mole hunt that rewards patience.
briefs.distinctive: Smiley is brought back to find a traitor inside the Circus; the suspense is institutional.
briefs.reservation: The first third is dense. If you want a set-piece every chapter, wait.
beats: The hunt is inside the service.
briefs.rights: Typography or handwritten Remotion only. No retailer cover. No film stills.
briefs.do_not: Do not spoil the mole. Do not use the 2011 film as the hook.

briefs.title: Four Thousand Weeks
briefs.author: Oliver Burkeman
briefs.hook: You do not have a time-management problem. You have a finitude problem.
briefs.who_for: Readers tired of productivity books that add another system.
briefs.distinctive: The average life is about four thousand weeks; the book argues for choosing, not clearing the list.
briefs.reservation: If you want a step-by-step planner, this will feel like philosophy.
briefs.rights: Typography or handwritten Remotion only. No retailer cover.
briefs.do_not: Do not turn it into a five-hacks list. Do not claim it will change your life.

briefs.title: Stoner
briefs.author: John Williams
briefs.hook: A quiet life that should not have been forgettable.
briefs.who_for: Readers who want a campus novel about work, not campus hijinks.
briefs.distinctive: William Stoner becomes a teacher, marries badly, and is barely remembered; the book treats that life as enough.
briefs.reservation: It is sad and slow. If you need plot machinery, this will feel uneventful.
briefs.rights: Typography or handwritten Remotion only. No retailer cover.
briefs.do_not: Do not call it the greatest novel nobody read. That is hype.

briefs.title: The Player of Games / The Three-Body Problem
briefs.author: Iain M. Banks / Cixin Liu
briefs.hook: Two huge systems. Very different front doors.
briefs.who_for: Readers choosing a first big sci-fi after a smaller book.
briefs.distinctive: Games and politics versus scientific mystery and cosmic scale.
briefs.reservation: Neither is a gentle on-ramp. Name which difficulty you actually want.
beats: Pick the door, not the ranking.
briefs.rights: Existing SciFi-05 Remotion or text-only. No retailer covers. No Netflix stills.
briefs.do_not: Do not rank Banks against Liu.
